If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{3}{5}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{(\frac{2}{5})}^{x-1}(\frac{3}{5}), & x=1,2,3… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X\ge 5.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & =1-P(X<5)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in {1,2,3,4}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & ={(\frac{2}{5})}^{0}(\frac{3}{5})+{(\frac{2}{5})}^{1}(\frac{3}{5})+{(\frac{2}{5})}^{2}(\frac{3}{5})+{(\frac{2}{5})}^{3}(\frac{3}{5}) \\  & =0.9744.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 5) & =1-P(X<5) \\  & =1-0.9744 \\  & =0.0256.\end{aligned}
$$
